complete_examples.text: From the calculated indexes listed in the table, the values of the vertical Sperling index for all ballastless tracks are greatly beyond the limit of 3, illustrating that the comfort and stability of running vehicle deteriorate in the soil deformation region.

When the vehicle passes through the soil deformation region, there are several indexes are not qualified, i.e., the Sperling index, wheel unloading rate and Rail vertical displacement, which should be taken into account for guaranteeing the better working state of the VTS system.
Similarly, the evolution of the CDS has little effect on the lateral Sperling index.
Similar to the evolution curve of maximum accelerations, the vertical Sperling index is enlarged with the evolution of CDS.
The maximum rail displacements, the maximum derailment coefficient, the maximum wheel load reduction rate, and the Sperling index varying with the different months are shown in Fig. 17.
The Sperling index [47] is a vital index to judge the stability of the running train.

Furthermore, it is interesting to note that the Sperling index under full probability track irregularity covers its values with any probability level, however, the PDF curve with the full-probability level becomes flatter compared with the deterministic probability level, and the comfort index is also the same.
The Sperling index presented in the China specification “GB/T 5599-2019” (Specification for dynamic performance assessment and testing verification of rolling stock, 2019) is selected as the basis.
According to the specification, the Sperling index needs to be less than 3.
